text:
Alex Chen: Quick sync — I opened a PR that adds customer-scoped feature toggles for enterprise accounts. Need alignment on allowlist semantics, contract gating rules, and who runs the manual enable for VIPs.

Priya Nair: Awesome. What's the intended default behavior for customers not on the allowlist? Opt-out (off) right?

Alex Chen: Yes — default off. Only customers explicitly in the allowlist OR matching a contract gate should get enabled. We also want a tiny canary path for live testing.

Marco Silva: +1. Can we embed the contract gating check as: contract has feature flag = true OR plan >= enterprise? That would let sales-activated toggles work.

Priya Nair: That works. Need to confirm how this maps to entitlement records in billing. I'll follow up with Billing.

Samir Gupta: Suggest adding an explicit VIP tag for tricky customers (manual override), because some enterprise deals want immediate access before contract fields are backfilled.

Alex Chen: Good call. Proposed config format (in PR description) — example:

```json
{
  "flag": "fast-kv-cache",
  "scope": "customer",
  "allowlist": ["cust-00123", "cust-00987"],
  "contract_gate": {
    "min_plan": "enterprise",
    "required_flag": "embedding_cache_allowed"
  },
  "vip_allowlist": ["cust-77777"],
  "canary": { "percent": 0.05 },
  "guardrails": {
    "max_error_rate_pct": 3,
    "p95_latency_ms": 1200
  }
}
```

Alex Chen: Implementation notes: the runtime checks in this order — vip_allowlist -> allowlist -> contract_gate -> canary rollout. Canary should randomly opt-in 5% of traffic for non-entitled customers and be per-customer consistent (hash on customer_id).

Dana Ortiz: Who has permission to flip vip_allowlist? Ops console only? I can run it, but we should list owners.

Alex Chen: Ops + product manager. Dana, can you own the runbook entry and the toggle process?

Dana Ortiz: Yep. I'll add a step-by-step and required approvals. Will include the API curl example: 

```bash
curl -X POST "https://console.redwood.ai/api/flags/toggle" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"flag":"fast-kv-cache","action":"vip_add","customer_id":"cust-77777","reason":"VIP enable for P0 support"}'
```

Priya Nair: Guardrails — we should auto-roll back on spike: if error rate > 3% for 10m OR p95 latency increases by >30% relative to baseline, then auto-disable for newly enabled customers and page oncall.

Samir Gupta: Can rollout-bot be wired to monitor that and revert automatically?

rollout-bot: Configured. I can watch metrics (error_rate, p95_latency) for the flag namespace and trigger revert if thresholds are hit. Add the flag name to bot config.

Marco Silva: For A/B canary consistency, use stable hashing (mur-128 or sha1 mod 10000) of customer_id so the same customers get consistent exposure. Document that in the SDK.

Alex Chen: Need code review folks: @Marco Silva (runtime), @Priya Nair (product gating), @Dana Ortiz (ops). Ping me when reviews are done so I can schedule a small canary tomorrow morning.

Priya Nair: I'll review the contract gating logic against billing records by EOD.

Dana Ortiz: I'll draft the runbook and add the emergency rollback steps, plus the list of who can approve VIPs.

Samir Gupta: I'll add tests to ensure vip_allowlist overrides allowlist/contract gate and that canary percent honors the per-customer hash.

Alex Chen: Thanks everyone. Action items:
- Priya: confirm entitlement mapping to contract_gate (due EOD)
- Marco: review runtime PR + hashing recommendation
- Samir: unit + integration tests for scoping logic
- Dana: runbook + toggle perms + chore to add flag to rollout-bot

Alex Chen: Leaving the PR link here: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/482 (please comment on code paths and guardrail thresholds). Trying to avoid a broad enable without these checks. :thumbsup:

Priya Nair: LGTM for approach, will comment on the PR with billing caveats.

Dana Ortiz: I'll take the first manual VIP enable tomorrow if needed.

Marco Silva: Reviewing now, should be able to approve after a small tweak.

rollout-bot: Scheduled canary monitoring window: 2026-04-03 09:00 - 12:00 UTC for flag fast-kv-cache. Auto-revert thresholds: error_rate > 3% (10m), p95 > 1.3x baseline (10m).

Alex Chen: Perfect. We'll coordinate the canary start in #eng-oncall when everything's green.

Samir Gupta: One last note — ensure logs annotate whether a request was served via vip/allowlist/contract/canary for offline analysis (add header x-rw-flag-scope). I'll add that to the PR.

Alex Chen: Great, thanks. Closing the async thread — will follow up with PR updates and the runbook link. :rocket:
